rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM Employee e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Customer c WHERE c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId) LIMIT 50

SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_first_purchase_2010 FROM (SELECT CustomerId, MIN(InvoiceDate) AS first_date FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) WHERE first_date >= '2010-01-01' AND first_date < '2011-01-01'
rows.note: Assumption: a customer's first purchase is their earliest invoice date, and I'm counting customers whose earliest invoice falls in 2010.

rows.sql: SELECT a.Title, ROUND(SUM(t.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 1) AS minutes FROM Album a JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = a.AlbumId GROUP BY a.AlbumId, a.Title ORDER BY SUM(t.Milliseconds) DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assumption: total running time is the sum of Track.Milliseconds per album, converted to minutes (ms / 60000).

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS yr, SUM(Total) AS revenue
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY yr
)
SELECT yr, revenue,
  ROUND((revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY yr)) * 100.0 / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY yr), 1) AS yoy_pct_change
FROM yearly
ORDER BY yr;

WITH cust AS (
  SELECT c.CustomerId, COALESCE(SUM(i.Total), 0) AS spent
  FROM Customer c
  LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
  GROUP BY c.CustomerId
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_above_average
FROM cust
WHERE spent > (SELECT AVG(spent) FROM cust);
rows.note: I'll compare each customer's total invoice spend against the average of those per-customer totals, counting customers with no invoices as zero spend.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT p.PlaylistId, p.Name, COUNT(DISTINCT al.ArtistId) AS artist_count
  FROM Playlist p
  JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId
  JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId
  JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
  GROUP BY p.PlaylistId, p.Name
)
SELECT Name, artist_count
FROM counts
WHERE artist_count = (SELECT MAX(artist_count) FROM counts);
rows.note: I'm assuming an artist is linked to a track through its album, and I'm returning every playlist tied for the highest distinct-artist count.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM (SELECT il.InvoiceId FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId GROUP BY il.InvoiceId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 1) AS multi;
rows.note: Assumption: an invoice "contains" a genre if one of its InvoiceLine tracks has that GenreId, and I'm counting invoices with at least two distinct genres.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS SupportRep, SUM(i.Total) AS Revenue2010 FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId WHERE i.InvoiceDate LIKE '2010%' GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName ORDER BY Revenue2010 DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumption: the support rep is the employee in `Customer.SupportRepId`, and 2010 invoices are those whose `InvoiceDate` starts with `2010`.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_orders FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL AND RequiredDate IS NOT NULL AND ShippedDate > RequiredDate;
rows.note: I'm counting orders where ShippedDate is later than RequiredDate, excluding orders with no ShippedDate.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(ShippedDate) - julianday(OrderDate)), 1) AS avg_days_to_ship FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL;
rows.note: I'm assuming "shipped orders" means rows where ShippedDate is not null, and that the dates are in a format SQLite's `julianday` can parse.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS products_below_reorder FROM Products WHERE Discontinued = '0' AND UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel

SELECT c.Country, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount FROM Orders o JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2019-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2020-01-01' GROUP BY c.Country ORDER BY OrderCount DESC LIMIT 50

SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.CategoryName = 'Beverages' THEN od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) / SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 1) AS beverages_pct FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE substr(o.OrderDate,1,4) = '2023';

SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_with_orders_every_month_2020
FROM (
  SELECT CustomerID
  FROM Orders
  WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2020'
  GROUP BY CustomerID
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%m', OrderDate)) = 12
) t;

WITH order_values AS (
  SELECT o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS order_value
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS employee_name,
       AVG(ov.order_value) AS avg_order_value,
       COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM order_values ov
JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = ov.EmployeeID
GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName
ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I'm treating each order's value as the sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over its lines, then averaging those values per employee.

rows.sql: SELECT s.CompanyName, ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS Revenue FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = p.SupplierID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2018-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2019-01-01' GROUP BY s.SupplierID, s.CompanyName ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: I'm assuming revenue means UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from Order Details, and that 2018 is based on OrderDate.
